title: Priority-driven request triage and queueing for overloaded dependencies
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During regional spikes and upstream incidents, heavy tails on Redis/Kafka/Postgres cause cascading latency and token-cost spikes for customer requests. Current defenses are ad-hoc: timeouts and global aborts. We need a reproducible, tenant-aware triage layer that prioritizes requests, avoids head-of-line blocking, and provides safe fallbacks without violating SLOs for high-priority traffic.

Scope: implement an application-level request triage and queueing layer + upgrade existing dependency guards. Scope covers: Redis (hot keys/prefixes), Kafka consumer latency spikes, and Postgres write/read contention. This ticket delivers the core algorithm, metrics, rollout plan, and an operational playbook for on-call.

Goals:
- Keep P99 latency for paid/enterprise tenants within SLOs during downstream overload.
- Prevent long tails and unbounded queue growth that cause retries and cost amplification.
- Provide deterministic fallbacks (stale-cache reads, degrade to summarization, or best-effort async) for lower-priority requests.

High-level approach:
1) Priority labels: requests are tagged at edge with a priority class (critical, standard, background) based on tenant plan, route, and SLA.
2) Admission control: implement a per-host and global admission gate that uses token-bucket + dynamic watermarks to accept/queue/reject.
3) Queueing strategy: short in-memory priority queues with bounded depth and time-to-live; lower-priority requests are subject to early-eviction policy (age-based + score-based).
4) Degradation policies: per-route configured fallback chains (stale-cache -> cheap-model -> async-write). Each policy versioned for safe rollouts.
5) Downstream isolation: lightweight isolation wrappers around Redis/Kafka/Postgres with fast failure signals and adaptive cooldown timers to avoid thrash.
6) Circuit orchestration: integrate existing circuit breakers but change topology to prefer fast fail for background classes and graceful slowdown for critical classes.

Non-goals: full rewrite of connection pool manager; deep kernel-level batching changes. Those may be follow-ups.

Success metrics (initial):
- During a controlled downstream overload run, P99 latency for critical class degrades no more than 1.5x baseline and error rate increase <= 0.5%.
- Queue depth never exceeds configured capacity and 95% of queued critical requests are served within 200ms of admission.
- Observability: new dashboard with per-class admitted/rejected/evicted counters and heatmap of dependency cooldown events.
acceptance_criteria: Edge assigns priority class for >=95% of traffic and it is propagated through request headers.
Admission gate implemented with per-class counters, capacity limits, and eviction policy toggles in config service.
Fallback chains configurable in Console and versionable; at least Redis stale-read and async-write fallbacks implemented for one high-throughput route.
End-to-end test harness that can simulate dependency slowdown and verify P99 and admission metrics programmatically.
On-call playbook added to runbook with step-by-step mitigation actions and escalation thresholds.
Dashboard and alerts created: per-region per-class P95/P99, admission/reject/evict rates, dependency-cooldown occurrences.
Canary rollout plan documented and validated in staging with at least 3 canary shards across regions.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Initial writeup and proposal. Marking as P0 due to repeated incidents last quarter that affected enterprise customers.

2026-03-11 - Ravi Shah: Spike began to prototype in-memory per-host queues. Observed that naive queueing caused head-of-line blocking for background jobs; switched to deadline-based eviction which improved critical throughput in local tests.

2026-03-12 - Priya Iyer (SRE): Suggest adding a global emergency mode that forces aggressive eviction for background class and opens a fast fail pathway for async-only routes. Also requested explicit safety net to never evict critical class.
2026-03-13 - Design review (Figma link in links): UX for Console fallbacks panel reviewed; UX asked for clearer copy for admins to preview effective latency/cost tradeoffs before enabling policies.

2026-03-14 - Ravi Shah: Draft PR opened for admission gate and eviction policy: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/10254. Tests included for eviction ordering and per-class counters. Requesting review from SRE and PM.
runbook_snippets: If regional Redis enters cooldown > 3x baseline errors, toggle emergency-mode: config.set('triage.emergency', true)
If critical P99 exceeds threshold and admission reject rate > 10%: roll traffic to alternate region and notify on-call SRE.
To rollback: disable admission gate via feature flag and drain queues by lowering admission threshold to 100% accept for 5 minutes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission counters, eviction ordering, and TTL enforcement.
Integration test in staging that injects 5x latency and verifies fallback chain execution.
Chaos experiment in pre-prod that simulates Kafka consumer lag and validates that critical class requests are not dropped.
operational_notes: Plan a 30-minute maintenance window for canary rollout to reduce alert noise. Ops will monitor per-shard admission rates and queue sizes.
Add lightweight tracing tags for triage decisions to help root-cause in future incidents (triage.priority, triage.reason, triage.action).
Budget note: minor increase in memory due to per-host queues; projected <2% host RAM for typical host types.
